title: What happens when we add up the powers of two?
description: The powers of two are added up one step at a time, and then one is added to each total. The new numbers are the powers of two again, because each power is double the one before.
teaching_notes: One idea: a total of powers of two plus one is the next power, and adding that same power again doubles it. Watch for students who add one to the powers instead of to the totals.

source: Figure it Out Q6 (Try This), p.8
video_script.why: The child builds running totals of the powers of two, adds one to each, and sees why the new numbers are powers of two again.
video_script.substitution: The numbers are the powers of two instead of three, six, nine and twelve.
video_script.anchor: boxes of powers of two joined in a running total, with one extra dot added to each total
video_script.payoff_line: Adding one to each total gives the powers of two again

final_answer.value: sums 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ...; adding 1 to each gives 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, ... the powers of 2
final_answer.spoken: one more than each total is a power of two

maths_rules: why: a total plus 1 is a power p; the next power is p, so the next total plus 1 is p + p, double p, the next power
video_script.design: Boxes of one, two, four, eight and sixteen dots join into a running total. One extra dot is added to each total and fills the next box of doubling.

<bookmark mark='pow'/>They are one, two, four, eight, sixteen and so on, doubling every time.
<bookmark mark='sums'/>We add them up, one, then one plus two, then one plus two plus four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Then we add one to each total. What numbers do we get, and why?

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, add the powers up one at a time. The first total is one.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>One plus two is three. One plus two plus four is seven.
<bookmark mark='last'/>One plus two plus four plus eight is fifteen. Then fifteen plus sixteen is thirty one.

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add one to each total. One plus one is two, and three plus one is four.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Seven plus one is eight, fifteen plus one is sixteen, and thirty one plus one is thirty two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: why: 7 + 1 = 8, and the next power is 8, so 15 + 1 = 7 + 1 + 8 = 8 + 8 = 16

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step three, see why this happens. Seven plus one is eight, and the next power to add is also eight.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next total plus one is then eight plus eight. <bookmark mark='dbl'/>That is double eight, which is sixteen, the next power.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the next one: 31 + 32 = 63 and 63 + 1 = 64 = 2 x 32

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the next one. Thirty one plus thirty two is sixty three, and one more is sixty four. That is double thirty two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: sums 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, ...; adding 1 to each gives 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, ... the powers of 2
